decisions.reason: The explicitly finite tuple (lambda_1,...,lambda_k) specifies its own index set {1,...,k}; it is not the N-indexed infinite real sequence of def-sequence. No lambda_0 is missing. Positive parts and the separately defined empty tuple determine the diagram uniquely, and column counting proves conjugation is an involution. The general sequence convention cannot invalidate this explicitly specified finite data.

For the empty partition lambda_1 is undefined, so the displayed column-product upper endpoint required explicit nonempty scope. This is a nonfatal boundary-presentation defect: the original item already supplied the correct R_t=C_t=S_0={1} case. Stated that case before the formulas and restricted those formulas to n>=1, preserving the full n>=0 definition. For positive size, disjoint row/column supports give unique factors and factorial orders; row-column intersections are singleton cells.

Step 1.4 concerns mu=(3,2,1), but its inequalities and candidate-node formula used lambda, whose second part is 3. Corrected all five lambda tokens in that step to mu and synchronized the step 1.4 claims in both owning contracts. This is a nonfatal variable typo: the listed nodes and resulting partitions were already correct. Direct deletion/insertion checks give the claimed removable/addable sets for (3,3,1), (3,2,1), and the empty diagram; no claim changed.

The title omitted the finite-group hypothesis and therefore overstated the result: for the additive complex unipotent action (x,y)->(x+ty,y), invariants are the x-axis and their map to the trivial y-coordinate quotient is zero. This is a nonfatal title defect, since the Statement explicitly assumes finite U and invertible |U|. Renamed the title to that exact scope. The average is an idempotent onto invariants, commutes with equivariant maps, and lifts each invariant quotient vector by averaging a preimage. Kernels and images restrict as claimed; applying this to Y->Y/im(f) gives the cokernel assertion. Finite parabolic radicals satisfy the hypotheses over C, with L-linear restricted maps. No AC is needed.
